# Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers.Core

> Abstract base classes that implement all 56 members of `IScheduler` on top of a single override: `Enqueue(IScheduled)` on `Scheduler`, `EnqueueAsync(IScheduled, CancellationToken)` on `AsyncScheduler`. `SchedulerService` and `AsyncSchedulerService` add the `Service`/`AsyncService` lifecycle; every class also exists as a `Disposable*` and an `AsyncDisposable*` variant - twelve classes in all. For each call the base class captures the execution context (or not, for `Unsafe*`), wraps the delegate in an `IScheduled` work item with its own promise, hands it to your override, and waits; you decide where and when to `Execute` or `Decline` it. Exceptions from the item reach the caller unwrapped, never your consumer loop. Targets netstandard2.0, netstandard2.1, and net8.0; depends on `Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers.Abstractions` and `Josupeit.Practices.Services`; lives in the `Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers` namespace.

Install with `dotnet add package Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers.Core`. All types live in the `Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers` namespace - not `Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers.Core`. Types:

- `IScheduled` - the work item your override receives: `IsCancellationRequested`, `Execute(CancellationToken)`, `ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken)`, `Decline()`
- `Scheduler`, `DisposableScheduler`, `AsyncDisposableScheduler` - override `protected abstract void Enqueue(IScheduled scheduled)`; no lifecycle
- `AsyncScheduler`, `DisposableAsyncScheduler`, `AsyncDisposableAsyncScheduler` - override `protected abstract Task EnqueueAsync(IScheduled scheduled, CancellationToken cancellationToken)`; no lifecycle
- `SchedulerService`, `DisposableSchedulerService`, `AsyncDisposableSchedulerService` - `Service` lifecycle plus `Enqueue`
- `AsyncSchedulerService`, `DisposableAsyncSchedulerService`, `AsyncDisposableAsyncSchedulerService` - `AsyncService` lifecycle plus `EnqueueAsync`
- `SyncEnqueueCallback`, `AsyncEnqueueCallback` - public delegates no public member uses

All constructors are protected and parameterless. `AsyncDisposable*` classes exist only on netstandard2.1 and net8.0. Every accepted item must end in exactly one `Execute`, `ExecuteAsync`, or `Decline`, or its caller waits forever. The delegate's exceptions go to the caller unwrapped; `Execute` itself throws only `OperationCanceledException` when your execution token is canceled, in which case the caller gets `ExecutionDeclinedException`. `Unsafe*` items run under the default, empty execution context. The `*Service` variants do not check lifecycle state before calling your override.

## Documentation

- [Complete reference](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers/llms-full.txt): the call pipeline, the who-sees-what outcome table, the twelve-class grid, declarations, three complete schedulers (single thread, channel, decorator), and common mistakes. Load this to write code against the package.
- [PublicAPI.Shipped.txt](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt): analyzer-enforced inventory of every public member on all frameworks; [PublicAPI.Shipped.netstandard2.1.txt](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers/PublicAPI.Shipped.netstandard2.1.txt) and [PublicAPI.Shipped.net8.0.txt](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers/PublicAPI.Shipped.net8.0.txt) add the `AsyncDisposable*` classes. `!` marks non-nullable and `?` nullable reference types; accessibility is not shown.
- [README](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers/README.md): human-oriented package overview as shown on NuGet.
